**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**I. Complete the dialogue below with suitable expressions chosen from those in the brackets. (5 marks)**

Nda: Hello, good morning my neighbour. How are you today?
Chi: I am doing great.
Nda: .......... you been to town one of these days? (Has, Having, Have)
Chi: No, why? I have not gone to town .......... last week. (since, for, ago)
Nda: The situation in town is not the .......... . (better, good, best)
Chi: What is happening in town? Is there any disaster?
Nda: More than a disaster. Most of the streets are .......... with garbage. (litter, littered, littering)
Chi: Really! What is wrong with the company in charge of clearing the rubbish?
Nda: The workers have downed their tools for unpaid wages.
Chi: That is dangerous for the people and the environment. .......... must be done and quickly too. (Nothing, Anything, Something)
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Ce dialogue teste cinq points grammaticaux : le present perfect interrogatif ("Have you been"), la préposition temporelle "since" (point de départ dans le temps), le superlatif "the best", la forme passive adjectivale "littered", et le pronom indéfini "Something" dans une phrase affirmative.

1. **Have.** "Have you been to town...?" est la forme interrogative standard du present perfect avec "you".

rappels_de_methode.competence: Grammaire anglaise : present perfect, since/for, superlatif, passif adjectival, pronoms indéfinis
rappels_de_methode.contenu_markdown: Ce dialogue teste cinq points grammaticaux : le present perfect interrogatif ("Have you been"), la préposition temporelle "since" (point de départ dans le temps), le superlatif "the best", la forme passive adjectivale "littered", et le pronom indéfini "Something" dans une phrase affirmative.

**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**I. Complete the dialogue below with suitable expressions chosen from those in the brackets. (5 marks)**

Nda: Hello, good morning my neighbour. How are you today?
Chi: I am doing great.
Nda: .......... you been to town one of these days? (Has, Having, Have)
Chi: No, why? I have not gone to town .......... last week. (since, for, ago)
Nda: The situation in town is not the .......... . (better, good, best)
Chi: What is happening in town? Is there any disaster?
Nda: More than a disaster. Most of the streets are .......... with garbage. (litter, littered, littering)
Chi: Really! What is wrong with the company in charge of clearing the rubbish?
Nda: The workers have downed their tools for unpaid wages.
Chi: That is dangerous for the people and the environment. .......... must be done and quickly too. (Nothing, Anything, Something)
questions.corrige_markdown:
5. **Something.** "Something must be done and quickly too" est la formulation naturelle dans une phrase affirmative exprimant une nécessité d'action.

### Piège à éviter
"Anything" s'emploie typiquement dans des phrases négatives, interrogatives ou conditionnelles, tandis que "something" convient aux phrases affirmatives : ne les confonds pas dans un contexte comme celui-ci.

### Conseil
Pour choisir entre "since" et "for", identifie si l'information donnée est un point de départ précis dans le temps ("since last week", "since 2020") ou une durée ("for two weeks", "for a year") : "since" + point de départ, "for" + durée.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**II. Complete the sentences below following the instructions given in the brackets. (5 marks)**
1) Some Cameroonians have taken the COVID-19 vaccine in order to stay safe from the disease, .......... they? (question tag)
questions.corrige_markdown: 1. **haven't they?** Une phrase affirmative au present perfect ("have taken") appelle une question tag négative avec "haven't".

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**II. Complete the sentences below following the instructions given in the brackets. (5 marks)**
2) "You must show your vaccination card against COVID-19 before access into our ministry". The minister said. (put in reported speech)
questions.corrige_markdown: 2. **The minister said that we had to show our vaccination card against COVID-19 before access into their ministry.** L'obligation "must" recule vers "had to" au discours indirect ; les pronoms/possessifs ("our"→"their") s'ajustent au point de vue du narrateur qui rapporte les propos du ministre.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**II. Complete the sentences below following the instructions given in the brackets. (5 marks)**
3) If the government obliges the people to take the vaccine, there .......... be widespread anger. (give the correct word to complete the space)
questions.corrige_markdown: 3. **would.** Le deuxième conditionnel ("if + prétérit, would + base verbale") exprime une conséquence hypothétique probable : "there would be widespread anger".

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**II. Complete the sentences below following the instructions given in the brackets. (5 marks)**
4) The company director cannot .......... the services of a secretary. (complete with the correct phrasal verb)
questions.corrige_markdown: 4. **do without.** "Cannot do without" est le verbe à particule signifiant ne pas pouvoir se passer de quelque chose ou de quelqu'un.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section A: Grammar (10 marks).**

**II. Complete the sentences below following the instructions given in the brackets. (5 marks)**
5) We couldn't buy the latest made android phone because we did not have .......... money. (choose the right answer) (not enough, enough, enough of)
questions.corrige_markdown:
5. **enough.** "Enough" se place directement devant le nom qu'il quantifie ("enough money"), sans préposition ni négation supplémentaire.

### Piège à éviter
Au discours indirect, l'erreur la plus fréquente est d'oublier de faire reculer le modal "must" en "had to" lorsque le contexte l'exige, ou de laisser les pronoms possessifs inchangés ("our ministry" au lieu de "their ministry").

### Conseil
Pour choisir entre "enough", "enough of" et "not enough", retiens que "enough" se place seul devant un nom dénombrable ou indénombrable ("enough money"), tandis que "enough of" s'utilise devant un déterminant ("enough of the money").
